messages:
Aisha (CSM): Quick sync: Acadia reported intermittent CloudTrail -> SIEM drops during high-load tests. Need to triage NAT egress, KMS access, and CloudTrail role permissions. @Jon @Samir @Maya can you pick owners?

Jon (Infra): I'll take NAT capacity. Initial look at their VPC shows one NAT GW per AZ; port metrics look saturated during spike windows. Lina, do you have any TCP connection pooling on the forwarders?

Lina (Customer): We use 10 Splunk HEC forwarders, TLS to ingest.acadia-splunk.corp:8088. No special pooling; certs were rotated last week which coincided with the failures.

Samir (Security): Two likely culprits: KMS key policy missing Redwood's service role (blocks rekey/data-key ops) and CloudTrail delivery role missing s3:PutObjectAcl. Check both before assuming network only.

Maya (SRE): Also confirm no restrictive outbound NACLs and that route tables point 0.0.0.0/0 -> NAT. If Lina can provide an instance id I can run a quick egress test.

Lina (Customer): Instance i-0a9f4c123 is available. No VPC endpoints; all egress via NAT. We're happy to do a maintenance window.

Jon (Infra): Plan: reproduce with a load generator, then either increase port capacity (add NATs or use NAT gateway scaling patterns) or split flows by target. Lina, can you temporarily rate-limit forwarders to reduce burstiness?

Samir (Security): KMS policy snippet I recommend (replace ARNs):
```json
{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Sid":"AllowRoot","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:root"},"Action":"kms:*","Resource":"*"},{"Sid":"AllowRedwood","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::REDACTED:role/redwood-inference-service"},"Action":["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],"Resource":"*"}]}
```

Aisha (CSM): Lina, adding Redwood's role and confirming CloudTrail role permissions are our top priority. Until smoke test passes this stays as medium renewal risk (flagged in tracker).

Lina (Customer): We can add the role during the window. Also want a rollback playbook in case ingestion fails after change.

Devex (Solutions): I'll prepare a concise rollback runbook and a curl-based smoke test: `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://ingest.acadia-splunk.corp:8088/services/collector/health` expects 200. I'll upload to the onboarding docs.

Maya (SRE): Suggest enabling verbose CloudTrail for 1h during the change and sending to a temp bucket `acadia-debug-<date>` with 7d lifecycle to limit cost. Also ensure S3 PutObjectAcl is allowed by the delivery role.

ops-bot: Runbook uploaded: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/acadia-egress-kms-rollout  includes smoke test and rollback steps.

Jon (Infra): Proposed cutover steps: 1) temporary rate limit on forwarders (Lina) 2) add Redwood role to KMS key policy (Lina + Samir) 3) increase NAT capacity or add second NAT per AZ (Jon) 4) run smoke test (Devex/Maya). 30-min window tomorrow 09:00 PST?

Lina (Customer): 09:00 PST works. Please include our oncall sylvia@acadia. We'll perform cert/key backups beforehand.

Samir (Security): Recommend scheduling key material rotation on weekend; if not possible, snapshot key ACLs before any change.

Aisha (CSM): I'll send the invite and update the account health note after the cutover. We'll move risk to low after 48h of stable metrics. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
